findings.title: Waterfalls render as flat, glowing-white stripes draped across island tops (not vertical cascades)
findings.what: On every tall island a bright unlit white ribbon lies nearly FLAT across the terrain, running from near the island centre out to the shore, capped by a white disc 'pool' at the lower end. It is fully self-lit: it stays pure bright white at NIGHT and is in the exact same position/orientation across the noon2, noon3 and night captures (i.e. it is static geometry, not a ship wake/projectile). It reads as a painted white bar / greybox artifact slashing across 5 of the game's most prominent 'hero' islands, immediately breaking the stylized-AAA illusion. SoT waterfalls hang vertically down a cliff face with mist; these do not fall at all.
findings.where: audit-noon3/12-parley-point-aerial.png (long white streak from centre to SW shore); audit-noon3/diag-topdown-old-maw-caldera.png (two white rods lying on the green); audit-noon3/09-kraken-tooth-aerial.png (white rod on right shoulder); audit-noon3/14-widow-s-watch-aerial.png; night-audit2/13-old-maw-caldera-aerial.png and night-audit2/12-parley-point-aerial.png (still glowing bright white at night). Affected islands: Crow's Perch, Old Maw Caldera, Widow's Watch, Kraken Tooth, Parley Point.
findings.root_cause_guess: src/client/core/Game.ts ~5152-5209 (waterfall builder). The 'vertical' ribbon is built between upper = surfacePoint(0.3, fallAngle) and lower = surfacePoint(0.94, fallAngle) (lines 5159-5160). That is a ~0.64*radius horizontal run (≈37 world units on Parley, r=58) versus only a few units of vertical 'drop', so each ribbon quad (corners at lines 5188-5193) lies almost horizontal on the surface instead of hanging on a cliff. fallMat (5163-5171) is emissive (emissive 0xb8e0f5, emissiveIntensity 0.32, opacity 0.78) so it self-illuminates at night; the white CircleGeometry foam pool (5203-5209, MeshBasicMaterial 0xffffff opacity 0.6) is the rounded blob at the end. The drop>4 gate (5162) passes because of the large radius span, not because the face is steep.
findings.suggested_fix: Sample upper/lower at CLOSE radii on an actually-steep face so the fall is dominated by Δy with a tiny Δhoriz (e.g. pick the steepest local segment, or use radii like 0.55→0.70 and verify horizontalRun < drop before drawing). Orient the ribbon quads to face outward from the slope. Drop emissiveIntensity to ~0 (waterfalls should darken at night like everything else) and keep opacity/foam subtle. Also fix the stream-channel formula at 5230-5231 (sx = lower.x + lower.x*0.06*t scales toward the island-local origin, it does not march down-slope toward the shore).

findings.title: Offshore reef rocks are near-black (0x282520) — flat unlit spikes on pale-sand islands
findings.what: A ring of sharp cones placed just offshore around every island uses an almost-pure-black material, so against the pale sand and bright turquoise shallows of the bone-biome / white-sand islands they read as flat black greybox shards dotting the waterline and beach, with no visible rock form or shading. Most jarring at Skull Cove and Gallows Sands (rows of black triangles poking out of light sand) and Smuggler's Rest. On green islands they hide, but on the pale islands they look like rendering errors.
findings.where: audit-noon3/02-skull-cove-shore.png (black cones on the sand and at the waterline); audit-noon3/02-skull-cove-aerial.png (black blobs ringing the shore); audit-noon2/11-gallows-sands-shore.png (black pyramids across the pale island); audit-noon3/01-smuggler-s-rest-aerial.png (dark shards at the shoreline).
findings.root_cause_guess: src/client/core/Game.ts 6067-6106 (reef ring). reefMatDark = MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x282520 }) (RGB 40,37,32 ≈ black) and reefMatWet = 0x3a3328 (line 6069-6070); reefGeoSharp = ConeGeometry(0.7,1.2,5) (6072); reefCount = r/8, placed on every island. At ~0.15 luminance under flat noon light these become black silhouettes on light sand. The taller interior spikes on rocky/mountain tops share the problem via spireMat = 0x4d4338 at line 6111.
findings.suggested_fix: Raise reef rock albedo to a mid grey-brown (e.g. 0x5b5348 dark / 0x6d6455 wet) with slight per-instance hue jitter and flatShading so facets catch the sun; optionally tint toward each island's rock palette (BIOME_PALETTES rock) so they read as coastal rock instead of holes. Lighten spireMat (6111) similarly.

findings.title: Tavern building is a plain flat-shaded tan box — reads as a greybox house
findings.what: The tavern is a single untextured tan box with a plain pyramid roof (its triangulation facets are visible as flat shading seams), a brown chimney, and two dark rectangles standing in for door/windows. There is no hanging pub sign, no lantern/warm window, no timber framing, no shingles, and no colour or material variation. As the social-hub landmark on four islands it sits well below the stylized-AAA bar and looks like placeholder architecture next to a Sea-of-Thieves tavern.
findings.where: test-results/bld/01-tavern.png (close-up of the tavern asset). Also visible as the small reddish-roof box beside the dock in audit-noon3/01-smuggler-s-rest-aerial.png. Taverns exist on Smuggler's Rest, Castaway Reach, Booty Bay, Parley Point (MapGenerator hasTavern:true).
findings.root_cause_guess: public/assets/models/tavern.glb is a low-detail single-material building, loaded verbatim by buildPropInstance('tavern') (asset registered in src/client/assets/AssetLibrary.ts:21; placed near NPC/tavern logic in src/client/core/Game.ts ~6825-6876). No signage, lantern emitter, or surrounding clutter is added client-side.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-author tavern.glb with timber-frame trim, roof shingles (or at least a distinct roof material/texture), a doorway/porch, and a hanging painted pub sign; register a warm lantern emitter at the eaves (reuse the campfire/lantern_post path in buildServerProps ~2554-2558) so it glows at night. Cheap interim win in code: add a sign board, a couple of barrels/crates and a lantern beside each tavern, plus vertex-colour variation on the walls.

findings.title: Skull fort (the map's single hero landmark) is monochrome light-grey and sits on a visible circular foundation disc
findings.what: The one 'fort' landmark in the whole map (Castaway Reach, marked with a skull on the battle map) is a uniformly light-grey, untextured little castle — one keep, two cone-roof turrets, a red flag — with no stone colour/material variation and no actual skull motif on it. It rests on a distinct light-grey circular base slab whose hard edge is clearly visible against the grass, so it reads as a plain greybox model dropped on a disc rather than a fortress rooted in the island. For the game's signature raid target it under-delivers.
findings.where: test-results/fort/01-oblique.png and test-results/fort/02-skull.png (grey keep + turrets + red flag on a light-grey circular pad); seen small and grey top-centre in audit-noon3/08-castaway-reach-aerial.png.
findings.root_cause_guess: public/assets/models/fort.glb — single light-grey material with a built-in flat circular foundation slab; rendered as-is via buildPropInstance('fort') (asset list AssetLibrary.ts:21). Its collider/footprint (src/shared/props.ts:32 fort capsule r5.2 h10, footprint 8.5 at :64) implies it is meant to be a large landmark, but the mesh is plain and under-scaled visually.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-author fort.glb: weathered multi-tone stone (darker, mossy), banners, and a real skull emblem over the gate. Remove or feather the circular base slab (add a rocky skirt / sink it and blend the edge) so it doesn't look like a floating grey disc, and scale it up (~1.3x) so it dominates its shore like a SoT sea fort.
